title: Which crew rules clash?

blocks.text: A utility plans an outage week. Its decisions are how many crews go to each district, each an integer in a range (`variables`, for example `{"north": (2, 6)}`), and its planners keep adding rules: caps, minimums, pairs of districts that share a depot. Each `Rule` has a name, a linear expression over the districts, a sense (`"<="` or `">="`) and a right-hand side; `add_rule` adds one to a CP-SAT model and returns the constraint. When a scenario has no plan at all, the planners want to know which of their rules are to blame.

Write `clashing_rules(variables, rules)`. Return the names of the rules CP-SAT reports as sufficient for infeasibility, or `[]` if the rules can all hold. Guard every rule with its own flag, assume every flag, and solve with one worker.
With $`D`$ the districts, $`[l_d, u_d]`$ their ranges and $`R`$ the rules, each with coefficients $`a_{r,d}`$, a sense and a right-hand side $`b_r`$, the model is

The solver reports flags by variable index; map them back to rule names. Every kind of rule needs its flag: guard the `">="` minimums exactly as you guard the `"<="` caps. A rule added without a flag is always on, so the solver can never name it: a clash between a minimum and a cap must name both. About twelve lines.

cases.says: an infeasible scenario names rules that cannot hold together on their own
a scenario whose rules can all hold names no rule
a minimum rule that clashes with a maximum is named along with it
